extra.reason: Verified via local Python 3.13 venv smoke test: vod_routes.router and xc_server.router both mounted and reachable (/api/vod/providers/ returns 503 not_configured via require_configured guard, not 404; /player_api.php returns 200 with real payload). test_upstream.router gated behind EPGMATCHARR_VOD_TEST_UPSTREAM env var, confirmed unmounted by default and mounted when flag set.
Added 'vod' to Tab type, tab button, and render block in EPGMatcher.tsx following the gn/emby pattern. VodManager takes no props. Verified with npx tsc --noEmit -p . — clean, no errors.

xc_server.py now validates every request against the Dispatcharr-side vod_xc_account_id account's own username/password (fetched via DispatcharrClient, 5-min cache, falls back to last-known-good on transient fetch failure). player_api.php's no-action handshake returns 200 with auth:0/1 (XC protocol convention); all other actions and the /movie and /series stream endpoints return 401 on mismatch. Verified live: bad creds -> auth:0 on handshake, 401 on get_vod_categories and movie stream; real Dispatcharr-configured creds (fetched from account 26 via DispatcharrClient) -> auth:1, categories/streams/movie playback all succeed.

xc_server._proxy_vod_stream now takes the full ordered list of active-provider sources for a movie/episode (vod_db.list_movie_sources_for_streaming / list_episode_sources_for_streaming, most-recently-seen first) and tries each in order, falling over to the next on connect failure or HTTP >=400, before returning 502 only if all sources fail. Verified live: forced the broken 'Test Provider' (invalid domain) to sort first for a 2-source movie -> logs show 'connect failed' on source 1/2 then successful OPEN on source 2/2, client still got a clean 200. _BEST_SOURCE_CTE (metadata path) and the new streaming-source queries both filter to providers.is_active=1, so deactivated providers are excluded from both.

Added deactivate/activate/delete for providers, delete for categories (cascades placements, not the movies/series themselves), delete for movies/series (cascades sources+placements+episodes via FK), and granular delete for individual movie/episode sources and category placements. VodManager.tsx wired with buttons for all of it (Deactivate/Activate/Delete on providers, Delete on categories, Delete on movies/series, X to remove individual sources/placements), with confirm() prompts on the destructive ones. Verified live via Playwright: deactivated a provider (excluded from streaming sources, confirmed via list_movie_sources_for_streaming), reactivated it, created and deleted a test category (cascade-verified — its placement disappeared from the movie's placement list), all with zero console errors.

rule_json format: {match: all|any, conditions: [{field, op, value}]}, fields name/genre/year/country/director, ops contains/equals/starts_with/gte/lte. vod_db.evaluate_smart_category() loads the whole movie or series pool (per content_type), evaluates in Python (fast enough at 12k+ rows), and auto-places new matches via the existing place_movie_in_category/place_series_in_category (idempotent, additive-only). New POST /api/vod/categories/{id}/evaluate/ endpoint. VodManager.tsx has an inline single-condition rule builder on the Add Category form and a lightning-bolt Evaluate button on smart categories. Verified live: created a smart category (genre contains Comedy) against the real 12664-movie pool, evaluated it, got 'Evaluated 12664: 1 matched, 1 newly placed', and the matched movie's placement + category name appeared correctly in the UI.

Built background bulk enrichment (bounded concurrency=8, movies then series, progress-trackable via GET /api/vod/enrich-all/status/) plus poster thumbnails in VodManager.tsx (collapsed row + expanded detail). Found and fixed two real bugs during the live run: (1) progress dict key typo (f'{kind}s_done' broke for kind='series' -> 'seriess_done' KeyError, silently crashing series tracking), (2) real data-shape bug in enrich_series -- this provider (best-streams.tv) returns get_series_info's episodes as a list-of-lists-per-season rather than the XC-standard dict keyed by season, though each episode carries its own reliable 'season' field which is now used instead. Also added return_exceptions=True to the batch gather() calls so one bad task can't silently abort the rest. Verified end state on the real pool: 12662/12664 movies enriched (12635 with posters), 2027/2027 series enriched (2026 with posters), 49952 real episodes pulled. The only 3 unenriched items are my own synthetic test fixtures (dead test provider URLs), not real data. Full run took ~11 minutes; re-running is near-instant since fresh items are skipped via the existing 24h TTL check.

Added providers.priority (INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, migration-safe for existing DBs). _BEST_SOURCE_CTE, _EPISODE_BEST_SOURCE_CTE, list_movie_sources_for_streaming, and list_episode_sources_for_streaming all now ORDER BY provider priority DESC, last_seen_at DESC (recency only breaks ties within the same priority). Exposed in VodManager.tsx: Priority column with inline-editable spinbutton per provider row (POST /api/vod/providers/{id}/priority/), plus a Priority field on the Add Provider form. Verified live via Playwright screenshot -- Priority column renders correctly with editable values.

Added _vod_catalog_refresher background task in main.py (same asyncio.create_task pattern as the existing _epg_warmer), re-importing every active provider's catalog every 6 hours, catching exceptions per-provider so one dead provider doesn't block the others. Verified live: fired at the 15s startup offset as designed, logged 'refreshing 3 provider(s)', and on the real Infinity provider pulled in ~9500 genuinely new movies the provider had added since the first import (confirmed these were real new titles across normal genre categories, not duplicate/matching bugs) plus a legitimate separate '4K Movies' quality-tier catalog (2618 titles) -- see epgmatcharr-9zp.8 for the follow-up design question on how to relate 4K variants to their SD counterparts.

Added _vod_enrichment_scheduler background task in main.py, calling vod_importer.bulk_enrich_all() every ENRICHMENT_TTL_SECONDS (24h), offset 45s after startup so the catalog refresher gets a head start. Cheap by design -- enrich_movie/enrich_series's own freshness check skips anything not stale, so most runs are a fast no-op scan except for genuinely new/stale items. Verified live: fired at the 45s startup offset, correctly picked up and began enriching the ~9500 newly-imported movies from the catalog refresher with zero manual intervention.

Created 19 genre-based smart categories for movies (Drama, Comedy, Thriller, Romance, Action, Horror, Documentary, Crime, Adventure, TV Movie, Family, Science Fiction, Mystery, Fantasy, Music, Animation, History, War, Western) matching the real enriched-pool genre distribution, plus a dedicated '4K' category (name starts_with '4K:', see epgmatcharr-9zp.8) and an 'All Movies' catch-all (name contains '', matches everything) as a safety net. Same pattern for series: 9 genre categories (Documentary, Reality, Drama, Comedy, Crime, Mystery, Animation, Sci-Fi, Action) plus an 'All TV Shows' catch-all. 31 categories total, all evaluated against the real pool.

Found and fixed a real scaling bug along the way: place_movie_in_category/place_series_in_category do one full DB round-trip per item, which timed out (>60s) when evaluating the catch-all against the whole pool. Added bulk_place_movies_in_category/bulk_place_series_in_category (one connection/transaction for the whole batch) and rewired evaluate_smart_category to use them -- catch-all evaluation against 24852 movies now takes 0.7s instead of timing out.

Also added categories.sort_order inline-editable UI (spinbutton per category row, POST /api/vod/categories/{id}/sort-order/) -- last piece of the original acceptance criteria.

Final verified coverage: movies 24852/24852 (100%), series 2214/2214 (100%) placed in at least one category -- up from 2/12664 (0.02%) at the start of today's session.

Found and fixed TWO independent bugs both driving this: (1) Tier 4 fuzzy: difflib ratio inflation on short normalized names sharing one generic word -- fixed via _fuzzy_trusted() requiring real length (>=10 chars) unless near-exact, plus adding us/usa to noise tokens. (2) Tier 3 callsign (the one actually producing the originally-reported match, found via end-to-end regression test): _CALLSIGN_RE matched any 3-5 letter K/W word as a 'callsign' (World/Was/Wild/Kind all false-positived at score 0.92). Tightened to real callsign length (3-4 chars) + cross-checked against GN Station DB's real call signs when available. Verified against all 5 documented bug cases (rejected) + real callsign (KABC) and real fuzzy (Discovery, WGN America) matches (still work), using the actual freshly-built gn_station_db.sqlite. Filed epgmatcharr-dr3 (P3) for a related but separate data-quality issue found along the way: the GN Station DB build itself has at least one bogus call_sign entry ('WORLD') from an overly loose regex in build_gn_db.py -- not in scope for this fix, harmless here since Tier 3's own tightened extraction already excludes 5+ char words before ever consulting the DB.

Confirmed true bug with much broader impact than originally filed -- not just 'WORLD', but a structural gap in _pick_callsign() unable to distinguish a station's own callsign from a network/brand name Gracenote lists as an alternate display-name. Live audit found 197 stations sharing brand names (ABC/NBC/CBS/FOX/PBS/CBC) and 71 distinct call_signs each shared by 5+ stations (worst: NINE/Australia, 126 stations), 2,177 of 35,639 stations (6.1%) affected. Fixed with the general/principled approach (user's choice): _clear_ambiguous_callsigns() in build_gn_db.py clears call_sign on any station whose value collides with another station's, post-build, self-correcting with no blocklist to maintain -- station_id/name/icon_url untouched so numeric-ID lookups are unaffected. Also tightened gn_station_db.py's own _GN_CALLSIGN_RE ({2,4}->{2,3}, same fix as sxi) since the original 'WORLD' case was a UNIQUE (non-colliding) bad entry that the collision-clearing pass alone couldn't catch. Verified end-to-end in production: manually dispatched 'Build GN Station DB' workflow (run 30014591968), log confirms 'Cleared call_sign on 2,178 stations', final count 35,639 (unchanged, since only call_sign is cleared, not the row), gn-db-2026.07.23 release published successfully.
